Messages.Author: Andrea Williams
Messages.Body:
Anyone else think it's funny (not ha-ha funny, but that weird kind of
funny like deja vu) that WoTC changes the name of Jyhad to "not offend
the Middle East" among other reasons, and then comes up with two new
clans playing off stereotypes of Egyptians and Arabs (the Followers of
Set and the Assamite). I don't mean to sound offended, but how is
portraying Middle Eastern vamps as the terrorists and asassins of the
gothic world going to help anything? Why, that would be like portraying
Italian vampires as mobsters (the Giovanni and their "corporate
interests"...I'm sure they're all legitimae businessmen)...

Andrea, Vecchia del Giovanni
Welcome to the New World Order...please check your mind at the door

>clans playing off stereotypes of Egyptians and Arabs (the Followers of
>Set and the Assamite). I don't mean to sound offended, but how is
>portraying Middle Eastern vamps as the terrorists and asassins of the
>gothic world going to help anything? Why, that would be like portraying
>Italian vampires as mobsters (the Giovanni and their "corporate
>interests"...I'm sure they're all legitimae businessmen)...

We did not come up with Assamites or Followers of Set; those are clans
created by White Wolf for the Masquerade, the game VTES is based off of.
The existence of Assamites is not really "portraying Middle Eastern vamps
as the terrorists and assassins of the Gothic world", as there are many
Middle Eastern vamps in other clans, and there are non-Middle Eastern vamps
in the Assamites. The Assamites are largely Middle Eastern for historical
reasons. Also, I don't see Followers of Set as playing on any stereotype
of Egyptians; White Wolf simply picked an Egyptian god to base the clan on.
